title: Grammar: Academic Sentence Patterns — Nominalisation, Complex Structures, and Register
grammarTip:
Академические конструкции предложений — отличаются от разговорных:

НОМИНАЛИЗАЦИЯ (глагол → существительное):
Razговорное: "We investigated..."
Академическое: "An investigation was conducted..."
"discover" → "the discovery of" · "develop" → "the development of"

ПАССИВНЫЙ ЗАЛОГ для объективности:
"It was found that..." · "It has been suggested that..."
"The results were analysed..." · "Data were collected from 50 participants."

КОМПЛЕКСНЫЕ ИМЕННЫЕ ГРУППЫ:
"a significant decrease in carbon emissions over the past decade"
"the relationship between economic growth and environmental impact"

ХЕДЖИРОВАНИЕ:
"may · might · could · tend to · appear to · seem to · it is possible that"

💡 Главный принцип: академический текст избегает "I" → используй пассив и номинализацию

grammarTable.subject: Nominalisation
grammarTable.example: "The government decided to regulate" → "The decision to regulate" / "analyse" → "analysis"

grammarTable.subject: Impersonal passive
grammarTable.example: "It is argued that… / It has been shown that… / It is necessary to consider…"

grammarTable.subject: Complex NP
grammarTable.example: "a large-scale, longitudinal, double-blind randomised controlled trial"

grammarTable.subject: This + noun
grammarTable.example: "This finding suggests / This analysis reveals / This pattern indicates / This raises the question"

grammarTable.subject: Active vs passive
grammarTable.short: passive for process; active for emphasis

rows.form: Simple verbs → nouns for academic precision
rows.example: "analyse → analysis; distribute → distribution; implement → implementation; investigate → investigation"

rows.form: Verb phrases → noun phrases
rows.example: "They decided to investigate" → "The decision to investigate" / "They found that X" → "The finding that X"

rows.form: Why nominalise? Allows economy, precision, and reference to prior ideas
rows.example: "This increase in productivity" (nominal) vs "Because productivity increased" (verbal)

rows.form: Common academic nominalisations to learn
rows.example: examine → examination; propose → proposal; conclude → conclusion; assume → assumption; demonstrate → demonstration

rows.form: "It has been argued/suggested/demonstrated that + clause"
rows.example: "It has been demonstrated that bilingual children show enhanced executive function." (who demonstrated this — implicitly: the research community)

rows.form: "It is widely accepted/recognised/acknowledged that"
rows.example: "It is widely acknowledged that the native speaker model is no longer fit for purpose."

rows.form: "It should be noted/emphasised/acknowledged that"
rows.example: "It should be noted that this sample does not represent the broader population."

rows.form: Avoids first person; focuses on the claim rather than the claimant
rows.example: "I found that…" → "It was found that…" / "We can see that…" → "It can be seen that…"

rows.form: "This" + precise summary noun creates cohesion and advances argument
rows.example: "This finding / This pattern / This suggests / This analysis / This limitation / This raises the question of…"

rows.form: The summary noun names what was just discussed
rows.example: "The intervention reduced anxiety. This reduction supports the hypothesis that…"

rows.form: Avoid vague "this" without a noun — it creates ambiguity
rows.example: ❌ "This suggests that…" (what does "this" refer to exactly?) ✅ "This finding suggests that…" (specific and clear)

rows.form: Common summary nouns in academic writing
rows.example: finding, pattern, limitation, result, issue, challenge, assumption, distinction, framework, approach

grammarExtra.title: Active vs Passive in Academic Writing

rows.form: Use passive for: methods, processes, procedures
rows.example: "Participants were randomly assigned to groups." / "Data were collected over six months."

rows.form: Use passive for: impersonal statements of fact
rows.example: "It has been established that…" / "A correlation was observed between…"

rows.form: Use active for: specific authors' contributions
rows.example: "Jones (2020) argues that…" / "Smith and colleagues demonstrate that…"

rows.form: Use active for: your own analytical moves
rows.example: "This essay argues that…" / "I will now examine three competing explanations."

grammarExtra.title: Informal vs Academic Register: Key Contrasts

rows.form: ❌ "Loads of research shows" → ✅ "A substantial body of research demonstrates"
rows.example: ❌ Loads → ✅ a substantial body of / a considerable volume of / extensive

rows.form: ❌ "The study is about" → ✅ "The study examines / investigates / analyses"
rows.example: ❌ is about → ✅ examines, explores, investigates, addresses, considers

rows.form: ❌ "It seems like" → ✅ "It appears that / It seems that" (no "like" in academic register)
rows.example: ❌ seems like → ✅ appears to / seems to / would appear to

rows.form: ❌ "Really important" → ✅ "Crucially important / of considerable significance"
rows.example: ❌ really/very → ✅ considerably, significantly, substantially, markedly

exercises.text: "The researchers decided to investigate the effects of bilingualism." → "___ to investigate the effects"
"___ ___ ___ ___ that the intervention significantly reduces anxiety." (passive: research demonstrates this)

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct summary noun after "this."
exercises.text: "The sample was non-representative. ___ ___ raises questions about external validity."
exercises.hint: "This limitation" = naming the non-representative sample as a limitation before saying what it raises

exercises.text: "Loads of research shows that…" → "___ ___ ___ ___ ___ demonstrates that…"
exercises.hint: Replace "loads of research shows" with formal equivalent

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct verb form for a methods section (passive).
exercises.text: "The participants ___ randomly ___ to one of three conditions."
"___ ___ ___ ___ that this correlation reflects a causal relationship." (premature to conclude)
exercises.correct: It would be premature to conclude
exercises.hint: "It would be premature to conclude that + clause"

exercises.instruction: Which is the correct academic form?
exercises.text: "The study is about how language affects cognition." → Academic version:
opts: "The study really looks at language and cognition."
"The study examines the relationship between language use and cognitive outcomes."
"The study is like, about language and the brain."
exercises.correct: "The study examines the relationship between language use and cognitive outcomes."
exercises.hint: "Is about" → "examines / investigates"; precise academic noun phrase

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct impersonal passive.
exercises.text: "___ ___ ___ ___ that the results cannot be generalised beyond this specific context." (it should be noted)
exercises.hint: "It should be noted that + clause" — impersonal comment clause

exercises.text: "It seems like the study has some problems." → Academic:
opts: "It appears that the study contains several methodological limitations."
exercises.correct: "It appears that the study contains several methodological limitations."

exercises.text: "They found that the intervention reduced anxiety." → "The ___ that the intervention reduced anxiety supported the hypothesis."
exercises.hint: "Find" → "finding" (gerund used as noun: the finding that + clause)

exercises.instruction: Which is the correct active voice for citing an author's argument?
exercises.hint: Citing specific authors: use active voice with their name

exercises.text: "Really important findings were ignored." → "___ ___ findings were overlooked."
exercises.hint: Replace "really important" with formal academic modifier

exercises.instruction: Choose the sentence with the best academic register.
opts: "Loads of evidence shows that bilingualism helps the brain."
"A substantial body of evidence demonstrates that bilingualism enhances cognitive function."
"There is lots of stuff about bilingualism and the brain."
"It seems like bilingualism is good for you."
exercises.correct: "A substantial body of evidence demonstrates that bilingualism enhances cognitive function."
exercises.hint: Formal vocabulary + active reporting verb + precise academic language

exercises.text: "The data showed a strong correlation. ___ ___ suggests that the variables are closely linked.", (this pattern)
exercises.hint: "This pattern suggests that…" = specific summary noun + precise follow-up claim

exercises.instruction: Which uses the impersonal passive correctly?
opts: "It is argued that by researchers that…"
"It has been argued that the model requires revision."
"It is arguing that the model requires revision."
"It was argued to the model requires revision."
exercises.correct: "It has been argued that the model requires revision."
exercises.hint: "It has been + pp + that + clause" = correct impersonal passive

exercises.text: "The government implemented the policy." → "The ___ of the policy had significant effects."

questions.text: "The ___ of these findings supports the central hypothesis." (find → noun)
"___ ___ ___ ___ that the intervention produced no significant effect in the long term." (passive: research shows this)
questions.hint: "It has been shown that + clause" — impersonal passive

questions.text: "The sample was small. ___ ___ raises serious questions about generalisability." (specify what "this" refers to)
questions.hint: "This limitation" = naming the small sample as a limitation before explaining its consequences

questions.text: "___ ___ ___ ___ that these results could be replicated in other contexts." (premature to conclude)
questions.correct: It would be premature to conclude
questions.hint: "It would be premature to conclude that + clause"

questions.text: "Participants ___ randomly ___ to one of four groups." (methods passive)
In academic writing, "loads of research shows" is an appropriate expression.
questions.hint: Register error: "loads of" is informal. Use "a substantial body of research demonstrates"

questions.text: "The ___ of the policy improved outcomes significantly." (implement → noun)
"Smith and colleagues (2020) ___ that higher sample sizes are needed." (active — citing specific authors)
questions.hint: Citing specific authors: active voice "Jones argues that…"

questions.text: "___ ___ ___ ___ that this is an unusually large effect for this type of intervention." (it is significant)
questions.hint: "It is significant that + clause" = impersonal evaluation

questions.text: Which is the most academically appropriate replacement for "The study is about…"?
opts: The study is kind of exploring
The study is doing research on
questions.hint: "Is about" → examines, investigates, analyses (precise academic verbs)

questions.text: "The results were mixed. ___ ___ raises the need for further research." (this inconsistency / ambiguity)
questions.correct: This ambiguity / This inconsistency / This pattern

questions.text: Which sentence has the strongest academic register?
opts: "There is lots of research on this topic that shows interesting things."
"A substantial body of peer-reviewed research demonstrates a consistent pattern across contexts."
"It seems like there might be some evidence for this."
"Really important research shows really big effects."
questions.correct: "A substantial body of peer-reviewed research demonstrates a consistent pattern across contexts."
questions.hint: Formal noun phrase + precise academic verb + specific claim = best academic register
